reasoning: Cross-section of corn stalk at node showing distinctive black discoloration of the node with degraded tan/white pith tissue. This matches Physoderma stalk rot's key diagnostic: black nodes at first or second node with pith rot. Distinguished from anthracnose stalk rot (which shows shiny black streaks on rind rather than black nodes), charcoal stalk rot (gray shredded pith with microsclerotia), and Diplodia stalk rot (which lacks the intense black node coloring).
